summary: The note describes Holographic Heritage Festivals, events that use hologram technology, scent machines, soundscapes and AI to bring historical figures and eras to life. The first one opened in Paris on September 5, 2023, and the concept then spread to other cities and into education. The piece covers the creators, the technical and creative process, interactive features, and the cultural impact.
one_line: Holographic Heritage Festivals, launched in Paris in 2023, use holograms, AI and sensory effects to immerse visitors in historical eras and have spread worldwide.
key_facts: The first Holographic Heritage Festival was unveiled on September 5, 2023, above Champ de Mars in Paris.
The concept was created by French historians and technology enthusiasts, including holography expert Dr. Odette Girard, to draw younger generations to their cultural history.
The organizers collaborated with Polispectra Tech Company, a trailblazer in the hologram industry.
The hologram of King Louis XIV took over three months to perfect.
Scent machines and orchestrated soundscapes accompanied the holograms, and cobblestone paths were high-definition surfaces simulating ancient roads.
Each evening focused on a different epoch, from the Roman Empire to the Versailles court.
Some holograms were infused with artificial intelligence so they could answer questions and hold simple dialogue.
On October 10, 2023, Sorbonne history professor Marius Dupont held a philosophy discussion with a holographic Voltaire.
Artist Elise Chevalier researched historical records, art and literature, and motion-capture technology let actors give life to the figures' movements.
By mid-2024, holographic festivals had appeared in New York (the roaring '20s) and Beijing (Ming dynasty scenes).
In Rome, Mayor Alessandro Vittorio announced plans for a permanent holographic installation at the Colosseum featuring gladiators and ancient citizens.
Educators began using small-scale hologram technology in history lessons.
Historian Rebecca Lynn, who contributed to the Revolutionary France script, said: "We had to strike a balance between engaging storytelling and historical integrity."
